summary: Defines managed objects for subnetworks using IEEE 802.4 Token Bus technology, as an experimental part of the MIB. It is now historic.

eli5.summary: It is a checklist for monitoring one old kind of network where machines pass a token to take turns.

questions: what is the ieee 802.4 token bus mib
what objects does the 802.4 mib define
what is octet time in snmp
subtitle: A catalogue of SNMP-readable objects for watching and controlling IEEE 802.4 Token Bus network interfaces.

tldr.problem: Network managers using SNMP had no standard set of objects for the state, settings and error counts of IEEE 802.4 Token Bus interfaces.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines three tables per interface (operational, initialization and statistics), plus identifiers for interface tests and a chip set, all registered in the experimental part of the MIB.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is now Historic and was updated by RFC 1239, so it is a record of an experimental design, not a current standard.

today: RFC 1230 is Historic and was updated by RFC 1239. It describes an experimental MIB, so read it as a record of how 802.4 Token Bus interfaces were once meant to be managed.

sections.title: What This MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 1230 defines an experimental portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing subnetworks that use the IEEE 802.4 Token Bus technology. It is meant for use with network management protocols in TCP/IP-based internets, and its header names the SNMP protocol.

It builds on the Internet-standard Network Management Framework: RFC 1155 and RFC 1212 for describing objects, RFC 1213 (MIB-II) for the core objects, and RFC 1157 for the SNMP protocol itself. The framework allows new objects to be defined for experimentation and evaluation.
sections.eli5: Think of a form with boxes that a network doctor can read to see how one kind of network card is doing. This memo designs the form.

sections.title: Three Tables Per Interface
sections.content:
The memo defines three tables. A managed system has one entry in each table for every 802.4 interface.

  • Operational table (dot4Table): state and operating parameters specific to 802.4 interfaces.
  • Initialization table (dot4InitTable): the values an interface assigns to its operational parameters when it is initialized.
  • Statistics table (dot4StatsTable): counters for the interface.

All objects sit in one subtree of the experimental namespace, dot4, defined as { experimental 7 }. They apply to interfaces whose ifType in the Internet-standard MIB is iso88024-tokenBus(8). Systems with 802.4 interfaces are required to implement all three tables alongside the generic interfaces table.
sections.eli5: There are three sheets for each network card: one for how it is set up now, one for how it starts up, and one for counting what went wrong.

sections.title: Addresses, Octet Time and Optional Objects
sections.content:
Two textual conventions are introduced. They change neither the syntax nor the meaning of any object; they only make the specification easier to read.

  • MacAddress is an OCTET STRING of 6 octets. A 16-bit address is written by setting its upper 4 octets to zero, so AAFF becomes 00000000AAFF.
  • OctetTime is an INTEGER counting time in octet times, where one octet time is the time taken to transmit eight bits. This follows the 802.4 habit of measuring intervals that depend on media bandwidth.

A few statistics are marked optional so experiments can show whether they are useful. If a later revision enters the Internet-standard MIB, those objects will either be removed or become mandatory.
sections.eli5: Instead of seconds, the network counts time by how long it takes to send one small chunk of data, so the clock speeds up or slows down with the cable.

sections.title: State, Commands and Statistics
sections.content:
The operational table includes dot4State, which reports whether the interface is offline, outOfRing, enteringRing or inRing (with other when the state is unknown). A manager can write dot4Commands to enterRing, exitRing, reset or initialize; no-op has no effect and is what a read always returns.

Other operational objects expose the next and previous stations in the logical ring, the slot time, the last observed token rotation time, and per-access-class target rotation times. The initialization table has a read-write twin for many of these values, plus dot4InitInRingDesired, which decides whether the station tries to join the ring right after initialization.

The statistics table holds 32-bit wrap-around counters such as token passes, token pass failures, frame check sequence errors, frames received with the E-bit set, frames too long, FIFO overruns and duplicate MAC addresses. The memo also defines identifiers for the FIFO path and external loopback tests, and one for the Motorola 68824 Token Bus Controller chip set. The external loopback test is warned to be liable to cause serious disruption on an operational network.
sections.eli5: You can ask the card whether it is in the circle of kids passing the ball, tell it to join or leave, and read a tally of dropped passes and garbled messages.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section consists of a single sentence: security issues are not discussed in this memo. Several objects can be written (the commands object and the initialization table), but the RFC says nothing about who may write them.
sections.eli5: The memo does not say anything about keeping strangers from pressing the buttons.

items.label: other
items.desc: State is unknown, for example because of an error condition.

items.label: outOfRing
items.desc: Interface is not in the logical ring.

items.label: enteringRing
items.desc: Interface is entering the logical ring.

items.label: inRing
items.desc: Interface is in the logical ring.
